Semicha. dichtiv lifne Adonai‏ vesamach, sheen semicha bevama:
Shechitat tzafon. dichtiv (Vayikra 1) tzafona lifne Adonai, veen tzafon bevama:
Umattan saviv. shete mattanot shehen arba. dichtiv behu (Shemot 29) et haddam al hammizbeach saviv, velo bevama:
Tenufa. dichtiv tenufa lifne Adonai, veen tenufa bevama:
Vehaggasha. dichtiv (Vayikra 2) vehiggishah el hammizbeach, veen haggasha bevama:
En mincha bevama. dizvachim amar kera bevama velo menachot:
Kihun. dichtiv (sham 14) vezarak hakkohen et haddam al hammizbeach, mizbeach tzarich kohen veen bama tzericha kohen:
Uvigde sharet. dechevan deen tzarich kohen en kan makom levigde sharet, divvigde sharet ketiv (sham 6) yilbeshem hakkohen:
Uchele sharet. devichle sharet ketiv (Shemot 28) lesharet bakkodesh, velo bevama:
Vereach nichoach. evarim shetztzelaan veheelan, en bahen mishshum reach nichoach. vedavka bammizbeach dichtiv reach nichoach laAdonai, aval bevama afillu tzelaan veheelan en bechach kelum:
Umechitztzat damim. chut hassikra lehavedil ben damim hattachtonim ledamim haelyonim. veen chut hassikra bevama, dichtiv (sham 26) vehayta hareshet ad chatzi hammizbeach, velo bevama:
Rechutz yadayim veraglayim. dichtiv (sham 30) bevoam el ohel moed yirchatzu mayim, velo bevama:
Hazzeman. im chashav al hakkarban leachlo chutz lizmanno:
Vehattame. af al pi shezzar kasher lehakeriv bevama, en tame makriv bevama:
Vehi bevet habbelia. kol zeman shehi bevet habbelia metamme vegadim, vechevan dimtamme vegadim metamme shenayim ufosel echad:

Hichnis rosho baavir hattannur. af al gav dekayma nivlat haof im bet habbelia shel haochel hakkol baavir hattannur, afillu hachi tahor, demechamat haadam lo mittamme hattannur, dechol hametammeim begadim en metammein adam uchele cheres. umechamat nivlat haof lo mittamme, deen lah tuma ella laadam bevet habbelia:
Hekiah o shebbelaah. hayenu perash. demishsheyyarda labbeten en lah tuma, ucheshehi letoch piv en lah tuma, delo yochal ketiv (Vayikra 22), achila bevet habbelia:

Hannogea bezav uvezava kulei. kol hane shave maggaan lemassaan dimtammeu adam letamme vegadim, hilkach chashive av hattuma kol zeman shello fershu, meachar dimtammeu vegadim, ulechach hannogea ose rishon vesheni ufosel shelishi batteruma:
Perash. mimmetammeav, eno ella rishon bealma umetamme echad laasoto sheni, ufosel shelishi batteruma:

Veechad hammassit veechad hannose. veaf al pi sheenan nogim. zav vezava venidda behedya chetive, dichtiv zot torat hazzav vegomer‏ vehaddava beniddatah. umetzora veyoledet nafka lan millazzachar velannekeva, lazzachar lerabbot et hametzora, velannekeva lerabbot et hayyoledet:

En korin. bammoed, ella kerovav shel met. leimmo uleaviv velivno ulevitto uleachiv velaachoto uleishto, ellu shiva metim shechayyav lehitabbel alehem. veal shear kerovim sheeno chayyav lehitabbel alehem en korin alehem bammoed. velo amran ella sheeno chacham o adam kasher uvaal maasim. aval chacham shemmet, hakkol kerovav, vehakkol korin alav afillu bammoed. vechen al adam hammuchzak bechashrut vachasidut. vechol haomed bishat yetziat neshama al kol adam miyyisrael, chayyav likroa vaafillu bammoed. ukeria al aviv veal immo hi bechol begadav ad shemmegalle et libbo, vekorea beyado umavdil sefat habbeged haelyona, vekorea mibbachutz, sheeno machnis yado tachat begadav keshehu korea, vesholel leachar sheloshim yom, veeno meache leolam. vechen al rabbo shellimmedo tora. aval al kol shear kerovav korea tefach min habbeged haelyon levad, vekorea bichli im yirtze, veeno tzarich lehavedil hassafa, veyesh lo lehachenis yado tachat begadav keshehu korea, vesholel leachar shiva, umeache leachar sheloshim. veen keria ella meummad:
Velo choltzim bammoed. chalitzat katef, shezzerootehen vechitfehen megullot:
Velo mavrin. seuda rishona, sheavel asur leechol mishshello, uregilim lehaveroto birchovah shel ir, uvammoed en mavrin ella kerovav betoch beto:

Veen mavrin ella al mittot zekufot. vaafillu betoch beto en mavrin oto al mittot kefuyot, shergilin bishar yemot hashshana kol kerovav umi shellibbo gas bo leechol immo al mitta kefuya laaretz, uvammoed en mavrin ella al mittot zekufot:
Veen molichin. hasseuda levet haavel:
Lo betavla. derech kavod:
Velo veiskutela. kemin shulchan katan shel kesef o shel zahav o shel zechuchit. vaani shamati keara shel kesef, shekken belaaz korin likara 451:
Ella vesallin. shel arava kelufa. shello levayyesh haaniyyim shebbain lehaverot sheen lahem tavla veiskutela:
Ufotrin et harabbim. notnim lahem reshut lelech miyyad:

Hattame al miktzat hammishkav. rubbo shel tame al miuto shel mishkav, nitma hammishkav. vechen rubbo shel tahor al miuto shel hammishkav hattame, nitma hattahor. velo chayshinan al miut mishkav, kevan derubba detahor verubba detame yoshev alav, divmiuto shel mishkav tuma nichneset, uvemiuto yotzet, kidkatane sefa nimtzet tuma nichneset lo veyotza mimmennu bemiuto:
Miktzat hattame al hammishkav. kevan demiuto shel tame hu, af al pi shennishan al kol hammishkav, tahor hammishkav, ad sheyyinnase alav rubbo shel zav:
Umiktzat tahor al hammishkav. kelomar o miktzat tahor afillu al kol hammishkav:
Tahor. ad sheyyishshaen alav rubbo shel tahor:

Vechen kikkar shel teruma. ammatnitin dilel kae, ditnan kol hannose venissa al gabbe hammishkav, tahor. vaafillu ochalin shel teruma, im nisseu al gabbe mishkav veyesh benehen davar chotzetz afillu hu dak beyoter kegon neyar vechayyotze vo, enan mekabbelin tuma min hammishkav, deen metamme acherim velo mekabbel tuma behesset ella davar sheyyesh bo ruach chayyim:
Verabbi shimon metamme vazo. hoil umekomah tame, metamme vehesset afillu davar sheen bo ruach chayyim. veen halacha kerabbi shimon:
Lo yatzak. seder hammincha, bitchilla noten shemen bakkeli, veachar kach noten et hassolet, veachar kach chozer veyotzek shemen uvolel, vehachi mefaresh beferek ellu hammenachot nikmatzot [daf 75]:

Lo yatzak lo valal kasher. kegon shennatan kol hashshemen shebballog bemattan rishon shehu kodem laasiyyatah. dei chissar shamnah amrinan beferek kamma [daf 11] shehi pesula. uvaggemara befirkin muchach ditzika meakkevet, umefaresh lo yatzak, lo yatzak kohen ella zar, demikkemitza vaelach mitzvat kehunna, aval yetzika uvelila kesherim bezar. velo balal dekatane, al karchach lo balal kelal, divlila vadday enah meakkevet. umatnitin hachi kaamar, lo yatzak kohen ella zar, o lo balal kelal, kasher:

Lo fatat. [kedichtiv] (Vayikra 2) patot otah pittim. af al gav divminchat machavat bilvad ketiv, hu haddin lechol hammenachot hanneefot techilla, kegon machavat umarcheshet umaafe, mitzva lefottan kullan veachar kach kometz. veze im lo patat ella kede kemitza, kasher:
Lo malach. kol hammincha kullah, ella hakkometz. deillu melichat hakkometz meakkevet hi:
Lo henif. beminchat chote uminchat kenaot ditunot tenufa:
Lo higgish. kedichtiv (sham) vehiggishah el hammizbeach. shehakkohen molichah etzel hammizbeach umaggishah bekeren deromit maaravit keneged chuddah shel keren:

Pittim merubbot. gedolot yoter mehaddin shemmeforash bahen minchat yisrael kofel achat lishnayim ushenayim learba umavdil. veitzterich leashmoinan petitim gedolot veaf al gav deashmoinan dei lo patat keshera. desalka datach amena dehatam hu deikka torat challot alehen, aval hacha delav torat challot ikka velo petitim ikka ema lo, ka mashma lan:
Velo meshachan. harkikim hatteunim meshicha, kedichtiv (Shemot 29) urekike matztzot meshuchim bashshamen, achar afiyyatan moshchan vechozer umoshchan ad sheyyichle kol hashshemen shebballog:
Beminchat kohanim keshera. shekkullan kalil kamohu:

Beminchat kohen hammashiach uveminchat nesachim pesula. lefi shehakkometz deminchat yisrael belilato ava, log echad shemen leissaron solet, uminchat nesachim veshel kohen mashiach belilatan rakka, shelosha luggim leissaron, kedichtiv beminchat nesachim (Bamidbar 15) issaron balul birviit hahin shamen, uveminchat kohen hammashiach hu omer (Vayikra 6) solet mincha tamid, hare hi lecha keminchat hattamid shehi issaron solet balul birviit hahin:

Vehen bolot zo mizzo. hakkometz bolea mimminchat nesachim umimminchat kohen mashiach, verabbe shamnan shel menachot hallalu al hakkometz umevattelot leh, vehave mincha shello huktar kumtzah ufesula hannikmetzet. aval minchat nesachim keshera velo have kerabbe shamnah, kevan shello middaat ervu hashshemen shebbolato batel legabbah ucheman deleteh. veen halacha kerabbi yehuda:
Hazzevach mefaggel et hannesachim. vehashshote mehen anush karet:
Mishekkadshu vichli. leachar shessamu otam bichli sharet, shehakkeli mekaddeshan kedushshat olam deshuv en lahem pidyon:

Divre rabbi meir. derabbi meir savar shennesachim mitpaggelim lefi shehaddam shel hazzevach hu shemmachshir umattir otan lammizbeach, vehoil veyesh lahen mattir, mitpaggelim bemachashevet chutz lizmanno. vachachamim pelige aleh beferek bet shammay bemassechet zevachim [daf 44] veamre shehannesachim en lahem mattir, lefichach en mitpaggelin. veen halacha kerabbi meir:
Mippene sheamru. kelomar mippene ma amru hoochalim vehammashkim vehammaddaf millematta tachat mishkav hazzav tehorim, mippene sheamru kol hannose venissa kulei:
Kol hannose. kegon ochalin umashkin umaddaf shehen lematta mimmishkav hazzav venosim oto veenan nogin bo, sheyyesh devarim chotztzim bentayim:
Nissa al gabbe hammishkav. sheellu lemala vehammishkav lematta venissa alav veen nogin bo, tehorim:

Chutz min haadam. shehaadam hannose hammishkav, nitma af al pi shello naga bo velo hissito, mippene shemmishkav hazzav metamme vemassa. vechen im natnu even mesama lemala mimmishkavo shel zav veyashav adam tahor al haeven, nitma, kevan shennissa al gabbe mishkav. keshem sheim yashav hazzav al haeven nitma hammishkav shellematta min haeven, kach kesheyyashav hattahor al haeven, nitma venissa min hammishkav shettachteha:
Kol hannose al gabbe nevela. beadam kamayre, kelomar vechol adam hannose venittan al gabbe nevela:
Tahor chutz min hammassit. denose et hannevela velo zaz mimmekomo gam lo heniah mimmekomah ella shemmunnachat al gabbav, kegon shebba chavero vehinnichah alav, tahor, ad sheyyassitenna:

Rabbi eliezer omer af hannose. baggemara mefaresh dehachi kaamar, vehu shennose, kelomar en hammassit et hannevela tame ella cheshennose otah, shennevela lemala vehu lematta. aval im hannevela lematta vehu lemala, af al pi shemmassitah, tahor, kol zeman shello naga bah. veen halacha kerabbi eliezer:

Chutz min hammaahil. sheefshar lihyot nose venissa velo yaahil, kegon aliyya mafseket, sheim hammet baaliyya voochalin umashkin vechelim babbayit maggiin ad sheme kora vehannesarim nichpafim mikkoved hammet umachbidin al hakkelim, o shehammet babbayit samuch lishme kora vehakkelim baaliyya venichpafim hannesarim shebbaaliyya mikkoved hakkelim umachbidim al hammet, bichhay gavna have nose venissa al gabbe hammet veeno maahil, vetahor:
Veadam bizman shehu massit. ben nose et hammet, ben nissa al gabbe met, tame af al pi sheeno nogea bo. aval im en hammet zaz mimmekomo, sheen kan hesset, tahor:
Veechad hammassit. hammeziz otah mimmekomah af al pi sheeno lo nogea velo nose:
Rabbi eliezer omer af hannose. vehu shennose kaamar, kelomar en hammassit tame ella im ken nose, shehen lemala vehammassit lematta. veen halacha kerabbi eliezer:
Veellu megallechin. habba mimmedinat hayyam. bammoed. shello haya lo penay legalleach kodem hammoed. vehu shepparas lischora o ledavar hatztzarich, aval im lo paras ella letiyyul bealma asur:
Vehayyotze mibbet haasurin. vaafillu chavush beyad yisrael, shehaya mannicho legalleach, lefi shehaya betzaar:
Umenudde. shehittiru lo nidduyo bammoed. vekodem hammoed lo haya yachol legalleach, dimnudde asur betisporet:
Umi shennadar. shello legalleach, velo matza chacham sheyyattir lo nidro kodem hammoed. i nammi lo matza petach lacharata ella bammoed:
Vehannazir. shehishlim neziruto bammoed:

Hachi garsinan, vehammetzora haole mittumato letohorato. im chal shevii shello bammoed muttar betisporet, dichtiv (Vayikra 14) bayyom hashshevii yegallach et kol searo. vegilluach denetek lo chashiv, sheeno ella davar muat shemmegalleach seviv hannetek. vetama deasur lechol adam legalleach bammoed chutz meellu hashshenuyim bammishna, kede shello yechavvenu legalleach betoch hammoed shehem betelim bo mimmelacha, veyavo yom tov rishon shel regel keshehem menuvvalim. vehayeynu tama nammi deasru hakkibbus bammoed:
Hakkometz et hammincha leechol. chutz lizmanno:
Davar sheen darko leechol. kegon hakkometz vehallevona:
Ulehaktir. chutz lizmanno:
Davar sheen darko lehaketir. hashshirayim sheddarkan leechol veen darkan lehaketir:
Kasher. deen zo chashuva machashava, divtela dato etzel kol adam:

Rabbi eliezer posel. dichtiv (Vayikra 7) veim heachol yeachel mibbesar zevach shelamav, bishte achilot hakkatuv medabber, achat achilat adam veachat achilat mizbeach, lomar lach keshem shepposelet achilat adam leadam kegon shirayim im chashav alehem leadam leachlam chutz lizmanno, vaachilat mizbeach lammizbeach kegon kometz im chashav alav lehaketiro shello bizmanno, kach poselet machashevet achilat adam kegon shirayim im chashav alehem lammizbeach lehaketiran chutz lizmannan, middeappekinhu rachamana letarvayhu bilshon achila shema minna ki hadade ninhu, umechashshevim mizzo lezo. verabbanan savre, lehachi appeka rachamana lehaketara bilshon achila, lomar lach ma achila bechazzayit af machashevet haketara bechazzayit. uleolam achila keorcheh mashma, kometz lammizbeach veshirayim laadam. vahalacha kachachamim:

Im yadua shemmiktzat hariyya mehayyom umiktzatah lemachar. sheraa ketzat reiyya besof hayyom uketzatah bitchillat hallayla shel machar, af al pi shello hayu venehen kede tevila vesippug, nechshavot shete reiyyot, mippene shehayyamim cholkin:
Vadday lakkarban velattuma. deyesh kan shalosh reiyyot, deotah shel ben hashshemashot nechleket lishtayim, kevan deyesh bah mishshene yamim:
Veim safek. deshemma chullah min hayyom o chullah min hallayla:
Vadday lattuma. dema nafshach ikka shetayim:
Vesafek lakkarban. dimsappeka lan shemma shetayim shemma shalosh. dei chullah min hayyom o chullah min hallayla, shetayim. vei miktzatah bayyom umiktzatah ballayla, shalosh:

Shene yamim ben hashshemashot. kegon derishona bitchillat ben hashshemashot rishon, usheniyya besof ben hashshemashot sheni, kegon haachat beerev shabbat bitchillat ben hashshemashot, veachat bemotzae shabbat besof ben hashshemashot. deim techillat ben hashshemashot yom vesof ben hashshemashot layla, en kan shete reiyyot bishne yamim retzufim, deshabbat mafseket veen kan tumat ziva [ella chevaal keri]. vei ben hashshemashot kullo min hayyom o chullo min hallayla, yesh kan shete reiyyot bishne yamim retzufim, vetaun lispor shiva nekiyyim ufatur min hakkarban. veim techillat ben hashshemashot o sofo chetzyo min hayyom vechetzyo mehallayla, nechleket hariyya lishtayim vechayyav bekarban. ulefi sheyyesh kan kol hanach sefekot, katane safek lattuma velakkarban, shemma en kan tuma, veshemma yesh kan tuma velo karban, veshemma yesh kan tuma vekarban. hilkach mevi karban veeno neechol:
En chofrin kuchin ukevarot bammoed. lehikkaver bo met sheyyamut leachar hammoed. kuchin, bimara shettachat hakkarka. ukevarot, bevinyan:
Aval mechannechin. sheim haya aroch mekatztzero. veim haya katzar maarich umarchiv bo:
Nivrechet. shel kovsin, makom metukkan lechabbes bo habbegadim, velet beh tircha kulle hay:

Vearon im hammet bechatzer. shemmet sham, muttar lenasser hannesarim velaasot lo aron. aval bechatzer acheret lo, shello yomru melacha acheret hu ose. velo shanu ella beadam sheeno mefursam, aval adam mefursam osin lo aron vaafillu bashshuk. uledidan sheanu mete mispar, kol adam have mefursam:
Rabbi yehuda oser. lehavi etzim laasot nesarim battechilla letzorech haaron, ella im ken menussarot kodem yom tov. veen halacha kerabbi yehuda:

Im yachol likmotz mizzo bifne atzmah umizzo bifne atzmah. shennafla zo betzad ze shel keli vezo betzad ze venishar mehen kede kometz shello nitarev, kesherot, veim lav, pesulot. deamar betorat kohanim missaltah velo missolet chavertah:
Lo yaktir. vaafillu kol hameorevet, deen haketara mitzva ella bekometz, umikkometz nammi lo kametz shene komatzim dilma bechol kometz yesh mizze shennitarev velekka kometz shalem mechad mincha:
Veim hiktir. kol hameorevet, hi lo alta labbealim, deha lo nikmetza veen minchat nedava nitteret belo kemitza:
Nitarev kumtzah bishyareha. lo yaktir et kullah, mishshum dehashshirayim asurim lehaketir, dichtiv (Vayikra 2) lo taktiru mimmennu ishshe laAdonai, kol shemmimmennu leishshim hare hu beval taktiru:

Nitma hakkometz vehikrivo, hatztzitz meratztze. dichtiv (Shemot 28) venasa aharon et avon hakkodashim, eno nose ella avon tuma, sheyyesh bah tzad kal shehuttera mikkelalah batztzibbur, dichtiv battamid bemoado vaafillu betuma:

Veeno meratztze al hayyotze. veaf al gav deyesh bo nammi tzad kal shehuttar mikkelalo bevama, shenneesar yotze bammishkan vehuttar babbama shebbenov vegivon shello hayu sham kelaim, af al pi chen en hatztzitz meratztze beyotze, dichtiv (sham) leratzon lahem lifne Adonai, avon delifne Adonai‏ in, avon deyotze lo:

Hakkol chayyavin biriyya. bemitzvat yerae kol zechurecha, shetztzarich lehitraot baazara baregel. vehakkol laatoye mi shechetzyo eved vechetzyo ben chorin. veen ken halacha, shemmi shechetzyo eved vechetzyo ben chorin patur min hariyya mippene tzad avdut shebbo:

Chutz mecheresh. veaf al pi shehu medabber, vaafillu cheresh beazno achat patur, dichtiv (Devarim lo) bevo kol yisrael leraot et pene Adonai, uchetiv batre lemaan yishmeu. perat lemi sheen lo shemia gemura. vehashshomea veeno medabber nammi patur, dichtiv ulemaan yilmedu:

Shote vekatan. delav bene chiyyuva ninhu, shehen peturin mikkol hammitzvot. vekatan sheyyachol leechoz beyado shel aviv velaalot mirushalayim lehar habbayit, aviv chayyav lehaaloto kede lechannecho bemitzvot, kidamru bet hillel lekamman bematnitin:

Vetumtum veanderoginos, nashim vaavadim sheenan meshuchrarin. kol hane imitu mizzechurecha, perat letumtum veanderoginos venashim sheenan bichlal zechurecha, vechol mitzva sheen nashim chayyavot bah en haavadim chayyavin bah. veod hare hu omer bevo kol yisrael leraot, vaavadim lav bichlal yisrael ninhu:

Hachigger vehachole vehazzaken vesheeno yachol laalot beraglav. mirushalayim laazara, kegon shehu meunnag beyoter. kol hane yalfinan lehu middichtiv shalosh regalim, yatzu ellu sheenan yecholin laalot beraglehem:
Vehassuma. dichtiv bevo kol yisrael leraot, keshem shehem baim leheraot kach hem bain lirot har kadsho uvet shechinato, laafoke suma vaafillu beeno achat, shehare en reiyyato shelema:
Shalosh regalim. harauy laalot beraglav chiyyevo hakkatuv, vechevan degadol patur min hattora, katan nammi lav bar chinnuch hu:
Shiva kene menora. kedichtiv (Shemot 25) veshishsha kanim yotzim mitztziddeha, vehakkane haemtzai, hare shiva kene menora:
Shete farashiyyot shebbammezuza. shema vehaya im shamoa:
Vaafillu chetav echad meakkevan. afillu ot achat shehi devuka lachavertah veenah mukkefet gevil kehilchatah, pasul bimzuza uvitfillin uvesefer tora:
Arba parashiyyot shebbattefillin. kaddesh vehaya ki yeviacha shema vehaya im shamoa:
Meakkevot zo et zo. ben bitfilla shel rosh shekkotvin kol parasha ufarasha biklaf bifne atzmo, ben bitfilla shel yad shekkol arbatan ketuvim biklaf echad:
Arbatan arba mitzvot. veen meakkevot zo et zo. veen halacha kerabbi yishmael:
Sheenah yechola. vechevan deze eno yachol veze eno yachol, kol chad vechad kulleh maase avid veikka rubbo shel zav nissa alav:

Rabbi shimon metaher. devae shiur ziva leze veshiur ziva leze, kelomar rubbo shel zav machbid al kol echad veechad. veazda letameh deamar leel befirkin bichidi tame, uvimrubbim tahor, sheen echad nose et rubbo. veen halacha kerabbi shimon:
Haya rochev al gabbe vehema. beomedet ayre, dei vimhallechet, kol shaa haachat neekeret veomedet al shalosh, vetame ma shettachtehen, sheenah yechola laamod al shetayim:
Sheyyechola laamod al shalosh. hilkach kol chad vechad have leh revii, veeno ella mesayyea, umesayyea en bo mammash. aval tallit achat tachat shetayim, temea, sheenah yechola laamod al shetayim:
Rabbi yose omer. aarba tallitot tachat arba ragle vehema kae:
Hassus metamme veraglav. im zav rochev alav vetallit tachat achat meraglav shel sus, temea. aval tachat yadav, tehora, sheen mishanto al yadav. veen halacha kerabbi yose:

Kelim shebbaekel temeim. demishenet hakkora al haekel. veekel hi hakkefifa sheotzrim bah hazzetim vehi asuya chemin kuppa shel maase sevacha, veachar sheotzrim hazzetim venishar haggefet shehu happesolet shel zetim, machnisin oto beoto ekel, venotnim al haekel kora lehachebid alav:
Hammachbesh shel koves. leachar shekkibbesu habbegadim, mekappelin otan tachat hammachbesh lechavshan velishmor kippulan:
Kelim shettachtav tehorim. sheen hayyoshev bekatze haechad shel machbesh machbid al hakkelim:
Verabbi nechemya metamme. savar i efshar sheyyeshev bekatze haechad shel hammachbesh shello yachbid al hakkelim. veen halacha kerabbi nechemya:

Hariyya shete chesef. gadol habba leraot tzarich lehavi ola, shenneemar (Shemot 23) lo yerau fanay rekam, veenah pechuta mishte maot kesef, shehem mishkal shishshim ushetayim garine seora min hakkesef hatztzaruf:

Vachagiga. shalme chagiga, sheamra tora (Shemot 12) vechaggotem oto chag laAdonai, kelomar haviu shalme chagiga, en pechutim mimmaa chesef. veaf al pi sheen lariyya velachagiga shiur, dichtiv (Devarim 16) ish kemattenat yado, chachamim natnu bahem shiur lematta, shello yavi pachot mikkan:

Hariyya maa chesef vachagiga shete chasef. dishlamim yesh bahem legavoah velakkohanim velabbealim, lefichach hen merubbin min haolot sheen bahen ella legavoah. vechutz meolat reiyya veshalme chagiga haamurim bematnitin od hayu tzerichim lehavi min acher shel shelamim, vehen nikraim shalme simcha, dichtiv (sham 27) vezavachta shelamim veachalta sham vesamachta. veshalme simcha hallalu lo huzkeru kan, velo natnu chachamim bahem shiur. venashim chayyavot bahen kaanashim, deal hassimcha nitztauu nashim, dichtiv (sham 14) vesamachta atta uvetecha:
Pundiyyot. keen kisin arukkin:
Learkan. sheshshochev learkan shel safsalim o shel pundiyyot:
Temeim. shekkol echad veechad nishan rubbo shel zav alehen, peamim al ze peamim al ze:
Lerachban. sheshshochev arko lerachban:
Tehorim. deen rubbo nishan al echad mehen, veen [tame] mishkav umoshav leolam, ad sheyyishshaen rubbo alav, dichtiv im al hammishkav hu, ad sheyyinnase rubbo alav:
Yashen. lerachban, vesafek im nithappech learkan, temein:
Kisyot. leshon rabbim shel kisse:
Shettachat hagguf. lefi sherubbo nissa alav. vehaacherim temeim magga hazzav. aval en lahem torat mishkav umoshav lihyot av hattuma letamme adam vechelim:
Im rechokim ze mizze tehorim. lefi sheen rubbo nissa lo al ze velo al ze. veen halacha kerabbi shimon:
Bau laggilgal. velo haya sham bayit ella yeriot hammishkan shel midbar:

Hutteru habbamot. derachamana amar asher yishchat bammachane vechulei‏ veel petach ohel moed lo hevio, perat laggilgal shello haya sham machane, shekkevar batlu hammachanot vehitchilu lihyot nefotzim bechol haaretz. umehay taama nammi kadashim kallim neechalin bechol makom, shehare lo haya sham machane kemo shehaya bammidbar:
Hakkol mittammeim beziva. hakkol, laatoye tinok ben yomo shehu mittamme beziva:

Af haggerim. dichtiv befarashat zav (Vayikra 15) dabber el bene yisrael, en li ella bene yisrael, minnayin lerabbot gerim vaavadim, talmud lomar veamarta alehem ish, lerabbot et haggerim veet haavadim. minnayin lerabbot et hakketannim, talmud lomar ish ish:
Umittammein bedam kaishsha. sheen haishsha mittammea beloven ella veodem, dedam ketiv bah, shehu adom:
Uveloven kaish. dezovo ketiv gabbe ish. vehu dome leme vatzek shel seorim:

Vetumatan besafek. im rau loven, shemma hen ishsha, veloven tahor bah. veim rau odem, shemma hen ish, veodem tahor gabbeh. aval im raa loven veodem keechad, tumatan vadday mimma nafshach, vesorfin alehem et hatteruma, aval en chayyavim alehem al biat mikdash, degabbe shilluach temeim ketiv (Bamidbar 5) mizzachar ad nekeva teshallechu, zachar vadday, nekeva vaddait, velo tumtum veanderoginos:

Rabbi yehoshua omer kippa shebberoshah. lirvuta nekatah, daafillu tzaif shebberosh hattehora nechshav keillu yashva alav hannidda, af al pi sheenah yoshevet alav. ufaleg assetam matnitin defirkin dilel delo metamme ella vigdehen velo chippa shebberoshan:

Kelim shebberosh hannes. ha nammi lirvuta nakat, deaf al pi shehem baggova berosh hannes shello vimkom derisa, afillu hachi temeim midras. uvisfina ketanna uvemitta machgeret ayre, kehahi deresh pirkin dilel, ella detanna dilel lo metamme chelim shebberosh hannes. veen halacha kerabbi yehoshua:
Bizman shemmassaan kaved temeim midras. veaf al pi shello naga vabbegadim, dechashvina la keillu nishenet al habbegadim:
Kesostera. kemo gezuzetra, kemin neser habbolet mikkotel haaliyya lachutz:
Venafal kikkar shel teruma. sheal hakkesostera:
Tahor. hakkikkar. veaf al pi shennafal mechamat hekkesh shel zav, la chashiv leh kehesset, mishshum dechochah shel kesostera yafe:
Vehi hayta nachala. haamura vattora ki lo vatem ad atta el hammenucha veel hannachala, demashma mishshettavou el hannachala yeasru habbamot:

Olot bammoed baot min hachullin. matnitin chassore michassera vehachi katane, olot nedarim unedavot bammoed baot, beyom tov enan baot, veolat reiyya baa afillu beyom tov, af al gav deyesh lah tashlumin kol shiva, ikkar mitzvatah beyom tov rishon, ucheshehi baa enah baa ella min hachullin. veshalme simcha baim min hammaaser, kelomar sheyyecholin lehavi shalme simcha mimmaot shel maaser sheni, deshalme simcha enan chova bemakom sheyyesh basar, vahare yesh lo meot maaser sheni lehotzi birushalayim, hilkach yikne bahem shelamim veyochal. aval chagigat yom tov harishon hu davar shebbechova afillu yesh lo basar harebe, vechol davar shehu mishshum chova eno ba ella min hachullin velo min hammaaser:

Beyom tov harishon shel pesach. hu haddin leyom tov rishon shel shear regalim. ulehachi nakat pesach, lefi sheyyesh erev pesach chagiga acheret, keshehayta chavurat happesach merubba hayu meviin immo chagiga kede sheyyehe happesach neechal al hassova, veashmeinan matnitin dachagigat yom tov atzmo hu deeno baa ella min hachullin, aval chagigat arbaa asar baa min hammaaser:

Uvet hillel omrim min hammaaser. baggemara parech ammay, davar shebbechova hi vechol davar shebbechova eno ba ella min hachullin. umeshane betofel, shemmechabber maaser im chullin umevi, im yesh lo ochlin harebe veen lo sippek bivhema achat, mevi behema achat lachagiga min hachullin vehashshear mimmeot maaser sheni. veaf al pi shekkol habbaot beyom tov rishon shem chagiga alehen, mikkol makom savre bet hillel demuttar lehavi hashshear min hammaaser, hoil uchevar yatza yede chovato barishona min hachullin:
Ochlin merubbin. bene bayit merubbin:
Mevi shelamim merubbin. shalme chagiga rabbim lefi haochlim sheyyesh lo:

Eser talliyyot. leshon rabbim shel tallit. veeser lav davka, daafillu elef talliyyot veeven gedola al gabban, veyashav hazzav al haeven, kol hattalliyyot shettachteha mittammeot moshav, demishkav umoshav mittammein tachat even mesama:
Kara hazzav tehorim. middin mishkav, aval temein bemassa hazzav:
Bichidi. mishkav echad:
Tame. shehare rov hazzav nissa alav:
Uvimrubbim. bemishkavot rabbot bechaf moznayim keneged hazzav:
Sheen echad mehen nose et rubbo. dechi karu hen, en rubbo shel zav nissa al echad mehen, ella kol echad mehammishkavot nasa miuto shel zav:
Piggel bakkometz. behaketarat hakkometz chashav al hashshirayim leachlan shello bizmannan:
Ad sheyyefaggel bechol hammattir. vehaketarat echad mehen chatzi mattir hu, deikka nammi haketarat chavero, sheen sheyare hammincha muttarim baachila lakkohen ad sheyyaktiru hakkometz vehallevona:
Beminchat chote uveminchat kenaot. sheen bahen levona, vehakkometz levaddo hu hammattir:
Shachat achad min hakkevasim. shel kivse atzeret. veen hallechem muttar ella achar sheyyishchatu shenehen:
Hiktir achad min habbezichin. vahare en mattir hallechem ella haketarat shenehem:
Rabbi meir omer piggul. desavar chatzi mattir nammi mefaggel. veen halacha kerabbi meir:
Hannose et hammerkav. benose et hammerkav ketiv kibbus begadim, velo venogea, veen nogea ella rishon bealma:

Hannose et hannevela. hayenu massit, denose belo massit, tahor kedifrishit leel. venogea nammi binvela, af al pi shehu tame, kevan delo metamme vegadim eno metamme shenayim ufosel echad, deeno ella rishon bealma umetamme echad ufosel echad:
Me chattat sheyyesh bahen kede hazzaya. metammein begadim bemassa aval lo vemagga:
Mi shello chag. shello hevi shalme chagigato veolat reiyyato:

Veyom tov haacharon. shemini atzeret. veaf al gav deregel bifne atzmo hu, have tashlumin derishon. vechag hashshavuot nammi af al gav delo have ella yom echad, yesh lo tashlumin kol shiva, middeakkeshinhu kera lahadade, bechag hammatztzot uvechag hashshavuot uvechag hassukkot, ma chag hammatztzot yesh lo tashlumin kol shiva, af chag hashshavuot yesh lo tashlumin kol shiva:
Mechappin et hakketziot. teenim shetuchin bassade leyabbeshan, mechappin umechassin otan bekash mippene haggeshamim:
Af meabbin. shennotnin otan zo al gabbe zo veosin otan kemin keri, sheyyihyu haelyonot meginnot al hattachtonot:
Haddashoshot. sheddashim vechotshim chittim ledaysa:
Haggarosot. sheosim gerisin shel pol:
Hem. haummanin:
Hechmiru al atzman. veen osin afillu betzina. veen halacha kerabbi yose:
Belo taase. hoil ureuyin lavo leachar zeman en bahem karet ella lav gereda delo taasun kechol asher anachnu osim po hayyom (Devarim 12):
Torim shello higgia zemannan. [keditnan bechullin (22:) mishsheyyazhivu kesherin, umikkamme hachi pesulin] detorim gedolim velo ketannim bainan:
Uvene yona sheavar zemannan. divne yona ketannim velo gedolim, ufesulim mittechillat hatztzihuv vaelach:
Belo taase. hoil ureuyin leachar zeman yesh bahen lo taase leshochatan bachutz:
Oto veet beno. sheshshachat echad mehen uva lehakeriv hashsheni bo vayyom, veasur mishshum oto veet beno lo tishchatu veyom echad (Vayikra 22):

Umechussar zeman. ben shehu mechussar zeman begufo shello haya shivat yamim tachat immo, ben shehabbealim mechussarim zeman kedimfaresh lekamman. utzericha leashmeinan pelugta derabbi shimon verabbanan bechullehu, dei ashmeinan bevaale mumin, beha kaamre rabbanan mishshum dimise, aval torim uvene yona delo meise ema modu leh lerabbi shimon. vei ashmeinan torim uvene yona, mishshum delo chazu veiddechu, aval baale mumin dachazu veiddechu ema mode lehu rabbi shimon lerabbanan. vei tana hane tarte, mishshum difsula degufa, aval oto veet beno difsula mealma kaate lehu ema modu leh rabbanan lerabbi shimon, tzericha. veen halacha kerabbi shimon:

Miktzat tame al hattahor. afillu etzbao shel zav al hattahor, o etzbao shel tahor al hazzav, o chibbure tame, kegon searo vetzipparnav veshinnav, kol ellu nikrain chibbure, af al gav delekka ella miut hattame al hattahor o miut hattahor al hattame, nitma hattahor, delo vainan sheyyinnase rubbo shel zav ella al hammishkav velo al haadam:
Umiktzat tahor al hattame tahor. devainan sheyyinnase rubbo. veen halacha kerabbi shimon:
Ulemirpeset. hilluch shellifne aliyya shebbene haaliyya holchim bo veyordim derech sullam lechatzer:
Veshafin et hassedakin. gaggot sheenan meshuppain tochin otan battit, uchesheyyesh sedakim bitchiyyat hattit haddelef yored babbayit veikka peseda. shafin, tachin:
Maagila. etz agol shebbo machalikin haggaggot:
Bemachalatzayim. keli ummanut shel barzel rechava keen kaf, velah bet yad:
Hatztzir. regel haddelet hassovevet betoch chor haaskuppa hattachtona shel petach:
Tzinnor. hachor shebbaaskuppa:
Vehakkora. korot habbayit mammash shennishberu afillu kodem yom tov:
Uvilvad shello yechavven melachto bammoed. shello yomar amtin ad hammoed sheen li melacha acheret veeese et zot:
Kevashim. kegon dagim virakot vechayyotze bahen shekkovshin bemelach vechometz:
Sheyyachol leachlan bammoed. sheyyehu nichbashin maher ureuyin leechol miyyad:
Yotzin yede chovatan. shel shalme simcha:
Bindarim unedavot umaaser behema. dichtiv (sham 16) vesamachta bechaggecha, lerabbot kol mine semachot, dikra lo bae ella simcha, veamar mar en simcha ella bevasar, vehay basar hu:
Aval lo beofot velo bimnachot. dichtiv vesamachta bechaggecha, amra tora ase simcha mimmi shechagiga baa mehen, yatzu ofot umenachot sheen chagiga baa mehen:
Kol sheenah yechola lehamit baadam. shehi gedola kol kach shekkesheole vah adam enah mitmotetet:
Hattahor makke et hattame. et hazzav:

Hare hattame nofel. shekken derech hammakke et chavero, im haya chavero nimshach haya hammakke nofel, ulechach nechshav ze hammakke kenishan al hattahor. vedavka leinyan tumat midras ayre, detahor hammakke et hattame, tahor mittumat midras. aval tame hu, shehare nishan al hazzav. vetame hammakke et hattahor, begadav temeim midras, dahave cheillu hazzav nishan alav:

Hazzav vehattahor. o veasda. etzim gedolim keshurim beyachad venotnim otam bayyam o vannahar, umesimin alehem nes umolichim otam baruach el mechoz cheftzam. uvilshon mikra keruyin dovrot, vaani asimem dovrot bayyam (Melachim 1 5). venikraim nammi rafsodot, uneviem lecha rafsodot al yam yafo (divrei hayamim 2 2):

O sherachvu al gabbe vehema. setam behema nichpefet tachat harochev, hilkach lo shena kochah ra velo shena kochah yafe, nitma hattahor uvegadav. aval ma shehabbehema massetet beragleha, en nissat mechamat harochev, ella im ken kochah ra, kidmuchach perek batra deohalot:

Af al pi sheen bigdehen nogim. sheen bigde hattahor nogim bevigde hazzav, mikkol makom temein midras, shehassefina ketanna dumeya deasda umitmottin, ufeamim shehazzav machria hattahor uvegadav umittammein behesset. veyalfinan tumat hesset middichtiv (Vayikra 15) vechol asher yigga bo hazzav, uchetiv (sham 6) ucheli cheres asher yigga bo yishshaver, ma bo haamur lehallan meaviro, af kan meaviro, sheen keli cheres mittamme vemaggao shel zav ella im ken naga bo meaviro, aval naga bo meachorav lo tame, umeachar shellamadnu sheen metamme oto ella meaviro, ma talmud lomar asher yigga bo, magga shehu chechullo, heve omer ze hesseto. ha lamadta shezzav metamme vehesset. veim haya tahor bekatze echad shel kora vehenia hazzav et hakkora bakkatze hashsheni ad shehitnoea hattahor shebbiktzato harishon, kevar nitma hattahor behesset venitmeu vegadav tumat midras im hen begadim reuyim lemishkav umoshav:

Haggashish shel mitta. kemin etzim arukkim shennotnim bemitta shel perakim, veal yedehen hammitta nigsheshet venidbeket zo im zo, ulefichach nikraim otan haetzim geshishin. perush acher, etzim shennotnim tachat kare hammitta shello yippasdu millachluchit haaretz:

Shehen machgirin. keadam chigger sheeno yachol lehanniach shete raglav keachat. kach ellu kesheyyoshvim alehem bene adam, notim lechan ulechan, mittoch kach nimtza nishan hazzav al hattahor, vehattahor al hazzav:
Beilan shekkocho ra. vehechi dame ilan shekkocho ra, kol sheen ikkaro rachav veav kede lachok bo rova hakkav:
O socha. dehaynu anaf ilan:
Shekkochah ra. vehechi dame socha shekkochah ra, kol shennitmenet baachizatah, shehaochez bah tomnah bechaf yado:

Al ilan yafe. afillu omedet hassocha beilan shekkocho yafe. vechol hane nichpafim tachtehen vechoved haelyon al hattachton venishan alav. uven zav shennishan al hattahor, uven tahor shennishan al hazzav, tame:
Sheeno kavua bemasmer. umittoch kach hu nichpaf:
Al hakkevesh. al haggesher:
Sheenan asuyin betit temein. mippene shehen nichpafim:
Verabbi yehuda metaher. veen halacha kerabbi yehuda:
Mippene shessimcha hi lo. veen mearvim simcha acheret besimchat haregel, dichtiv vesamachta bechaggecha (Devarim 16), bechaggecha velo beishtecha:
Aval machzir hu et gerushato. deenah simcha kol kach ella beishsha chadasha shello hayta lo meolam:
Veosa ishsha tachshiteha. kegon latet kachal beeneha, ulehashvot sear roshah shello yitpazzer, umaaveret tzeva adom al paneha, umaaveret sakkin al paneha shel matta, vechen kol kayyotze baze:
Shenniuul hu lah. tzaar hu lah. veen halacha kerabbi yehuda:

Shachat shene chevasim. shel atzeret, dichtiv behu (Vayikra 23) shene chevasim bene shana lezevach shelamim, veotan kevasim mattirin umekaddeshin lishte hallechem, sheen hallechem kadosh ella bishchitat shene kevasim, hoil vehuzkeku immo bitnufa. ushear kevasim shel atzeret, demusafim ninhu:
Leechol achat min hachallot lemachar. uzeman achilat hachallot eno ella leyom velayla, kedin mincha, shenneemar bah kachattat vechaasham:

Hiktir shene vezichin. lishte maarachot shel lechem happanim kedichtiv (Vayikra 24) vesamta otam shetayim maarachot, hayta al kol maarechet kaf achat sheyyesh bo levona kedichtiv (sham) venatatta al hammaarechet levona zakka. ushete hakkappot hallalu shebbahem netuna hallevona nikraim shene bezichim. vehallevona nikteret kedichtiv (sham) vehayta lallechem leazkara. vehallechem neechol, uzeman achilato kol oto shabbat shemmesirim oto min hashshulchan bilvad. veim beshaa shehiktir shene bezichim shel levona chashav al achat min hammaarachot shel lechem leachlo lemachar, kelomar shello bizmanno:
Otah challa. shel shete hallechem shel atzeret:
Veoto hasseder. shel lechem happanim:
Ze vaze piggul. shekkullan nechshavim guf echad:

Nitmet achat min hachallot. davka keshennitmet achat mishshete hallechem kodem zerikat dam hakkevasim, o echad min hassedarim kodem haketarat habbezichim, hu deifligu rabbi yehuda verabbanan. aval im nitma leachar zerikat haddam o leachar haketarat habbezichim, divre hakkol hattame betumato vehattahor yeachel:

Sheen karban tzibbur chaluk. baggemara massik delo mikkera velo missevara amarah rabbi yehuda lemilleteh, ella gemara aruch beyado. vechach haya mekubbal merabbotav sheen karban tzibbur chaluk veim nifsal chetzyo nifsal kullo:

rashi: Tachat avotecha vego'. lechol echad miyyisrael amar:
targum: Baatar avhatach yehevyan tzadikaya benach temanenun leravrevaya bechol ara:

rashi: Azkira shimcha. kelappe hakkadosh baruch hu amar hamshorer:
targum: Beidana hahi temerun nidkar shemach bechol dar vedar metul hechena amemaya demitgayrin yehodun shemach laalam uleolme olmin:

Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 3:43-5: Further, for another reason it is fitting that he not become angry: for he thereby nullifies the mitzvah to fear the glorious and awesome Name (Deuteronomy 28:58) - for whoever is before the king and fears him does not become angry before him, but is ashamed and afraid of him, and leaves all his affairs to the king, since it is in his power to repair everything, and perhaps that very disgracer is acting by the king's own authority, as King David, peace be upon him, said (II Samuel 16:10), "the LORD has told him to curse." And so Shmuel said in Nedarim (22b), in the teaching we copied above in the previous chapter, whoever becomes angry - even the Shechinah is not considered important compared to him - it is not necessary to mention his own soul, hewn from beneath the Throne of Glory, whom the angels honor, and his fellows, made in image and likeness, whom he must honor, since "who is honored? He who honors creatures" - but even the Shechinah, whose glory fills the whole earth, whom he must fear - and this is (Psalms 10:4), "God is not in all his schemes" - the explanation of "all" [kol] is that not one thought of his own thoughts is [directed] against the Name; and "kol" is like the matter of "you shall do no [kol] work" (Exodus 20:10), and there are many similar cases. And through this is explained what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 145a), that whoever has fear has humility and piety; see there.

And when a person takes to heart that all the causes that befall him all come from Him, blessed be He, since He watches over every single detail - for they said (Chullin 7b), a person does not even bruise his finger below unless it is proclaimed against him from above - he shall not become angry at the deed of the LORD. And of something similar to this King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 16:3), "commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall be established."

Further, for another reason it is fitting that he not respond to whoever disgraces him: the warning of King Solomon, peace be upon him (Proverbs 26:4), "do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you too become like him." And one must be precise about the doubling in his words, saying "fool" and "his folly." And further, the words "you too" are superfluous, since he already said "lest you become like him." And one can say that Scripture gave three reasons not to answer a fool. The first is precise in saying "according to his folly" - meaning that since he is a fool, the husk, which is his folly, has clothed itself in him to say those things, and he is like a barking dog, whom it is not fitting to be concerned about. And a second argument: "lest you become like him" - for since his words have had an effect within his own heart, causing him to cease from holiness and words of Torah, the husk has also entered his own heart, since out of anger he answered him - it follows that he becomes exactly equal to the fool, for the fool who became angry and answered in folly - certainly they did something to him worthy of being upset about, and his answer is called his own folly; likewise the wise man who answers him, because his words made an impression upon him, behold he is like him - for it is fitting that a wise man in the wisdom of Torah not let vain words make an impression on his heart, even if there be disgrace to him - and the proof of this is Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, when Aaron and Miriam spoke against him, it is written there (Numbers 12:3), "and the man Moses was very humble" - and the commentators explained that he heard and was silent and did not take it to heart to respond, and the reason is that from the abundance of his cleaving to the Name, he did not concern himself with responding to worldly matters, and the Name answered on his behalf. And a third [reason]: "you too" - meaning, the soul that is with you - and this is hinted at in the word "atah" [you], for the essential part of a person called "you" is the soul, since the body ceases and is lost and has no permanence to be called "you," and when a person speaks with his fellow, he does not speak with his body but with his soul, which sees and hears. And in the plural [implication] it hints that the Shechinah too departs, as explained in the teaching we copied from Parashat Tetzaveh, that from the angry person, his soul and the Shechinah depart.

And the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz wrote, on the mishnah (Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 4), "be exceedingly, exceedingly lowly of spirit," fitting words for this discourse - I saw fit to copy them here. He raised a difficulty, that the Tanna should have said "your hope is a worm," since he began in the second person by saying "be." And he, of blessed memory, resolved this by saying that pride is of two kinds, and corresponding to them two kinds of lowliness. One: the proud person who thinks that honor is fitting for him and that all should honor him, while he does not honor anyone, like a king and princes. And the correct attribute in this is that he honor every person according to his own level, and think that he and they were created for His honor, blessed be He, and it is not fitting to make use of His creatures, made in image and likeness - and this is the attribute mentioned above. And concerning this kind of pride our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (see Sotah 5a), the Holy One, blessed be He, said of pride, I and it cannot dwell in one place - and the reason is as I have written, that honor is fitting for Him, blessed be He, since there is none above Him, and this is what He said (Psalms 93:1), "the LORD reigns, He is clothed in pride."

And the second is one who disgraces people, insults and abuses them, since they are considered by him as nothing and void - and concerning this He warned, "do not despise any person." And the correct attribute is to be silent, not to respond to his own disgrace, and for this he must be very lowly in his own eyes, like mere dust, so as not to feel it at all. And for this the Tanna said, "be exceedingly, exceedingly lowly of spirit" - if others disgrace you, do not be dismayed by them and their abuse - and he gave the reason, "for the hope of man" - for that arrogant man who disgraced and abused you, tomorrow the worm shall consume him, and what is his disgrace to you? And this is the reason it says "enosh" [man] and not "adam," which would have been more fitting, since man [adam] is taken from dust - but rather it intended what was said, to warn the one who is insulted.

And consider, reader, this explanation, for it agrees from every side - and Isaiah, peace be upon him, aroused me to this explanation by saying (Isaiah 51:7), "listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is My law; fear not the disgrace of man [enosh], nor be dismayed at their revilings, for the moth shall eat them like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool, but My salvation shall be forever, and My righteousness for generations of generations." Behold, the Tanna mentioned the language that the prophet said, "for the hope of man is the worm" - but he first said, "listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is My law," for people of this level are few, since from the first kind you shall find many people who honor others, each according to his own level - but that one hear his own disgrace and be silent - there is not even one; and whoever does so shows the greatness of his own attachment to the supernal world, "with gods whose dwelling is not with flesh" (Daniel 2:11) - and therefore he shall not feel the disgrace of the world - and for this King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 14:29), "he who is slow to anger has great understanding," "every man," and so on (ibid. 19:11) - and in the mishnah "who is honored" I have explained this with the help of Heaven.

And so that my words enter your ears, I shall give you a parable of a man who had two pearls: one, beyond all value, worth a thousand thousand thousand gold dinars, and the other worth a thousand gold pieces - and the second was stolen from him. Is it conceivable that this man should grieve, when the other, first pearl remains, which lacks nothing? So too people whose souls are very holy, and who have come to perceive their [true] world in their lifetime, shall not concern themselves with the loss of the goods of this world, and all of it is like the peel of garlic in their eyes - they shall not rejoice at its increase nor grieve at its loss.

My masters and my geniuses, look and see: the supernal holy one, Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, for whose sake the whole world was sustained, and who was content with a kav of carobs from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve (Berachot 17b); and Elijah, peace be upon him, "girded with a girdle of leather about his loins" (II Kings 1:8), and his meal was a cake baked on coals and a jug of water (I Kings 19:6) - this is nothing but the strength of their faith in their Creator and the intensity of their attachment and cleaving to Him.

And for this the prophet said, "who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is My law" - for this attribute is found only in one whose 248 organs and 365 sinews desire Torah, which grows in his heart this supernal attribute of which they said (Avodah Zarah 20b), humility is greater than all of them, and it is what brings one to the Holy Spirit, as it says (Isaiah 61:1), "the spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good tidings to the humble; He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted" - and these are the ones who ascend to this great and wondrous level. And this is the conclusion of the words of the prophet, peace be upon him, "but My salvation shall be forever, and My righteousness for generations of generations" - for God, blessed be He, is destined to raise the horn of the insulted, who hear their own disgrace and do not respond.

And know that the clear proof upon a person, whether the Name is continually before him, is the fruit of the whole Torah, in saying (Deuteronomy 10:20), "the LORD your God you shall fear, Him you shall serve, and to Him you shall cleave" - lowliness, and its opposite is pride. And I shall give you a parable of this: two men each have a thousand dinars - one in a village where all its people do not attain a thousand gold dinars - there is no doubt that this one shall be proud among the villagers; the second dwells in Tyre, whose merchants are princes - this one shall consider his own wealth lowly in his eyes and count it as nothing. So too, whoever is far from the Name, blessed be He, and from His angels and His pious ones, is proud over those below him; but the righteous, before whom the Name is continually present, shall be lowly before Him, down to the dust - for by looking at the greatness of the Name and His angels and His pious ones from the beginning of time, they shall become very lowly in their own eyes - and one of the eleven principles of the Torah is, "despised in his own eyes and rejected" (Psalms 15:4).

And see the testimony of Solomon, peace be upon him (Proverbs 15:28), concerning everything we have said: "the heart of the righteous meditates on how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours forth evil things; the LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous." It means: the heart of the righteous constantly meditates on what shall lead him to humility and lowliness; but the wicked are not content with their hearts being proud, but even bring forth their pride with their mouths, so that they constantly "pour forth evil things." And the reason for this is that "the LORD is far from the wicked," and they do not meditate on Him; but the righteous - "He hears their prayer," since they are continually holy to Him.

And now I shall tell you what they said of one of the pious ones. They said that a certain pious man was asked, which day did you rejoice in most, in all your days? He answered: once I was traveling in a ship with merchants carrying fine merchandise, and in order to be alone with my Creator I went down to the back of the ship and lay there in the lowest place - and one of the young merchants arose and disgraced me in his eyes, spat in my face, exposed his nakedness, and urinated on me. I was astonished at his brazenness, but as the LORD lives, my soul was not grieved at all by his deed - and when he passed from my presence I rejoiced with a great joy, that my soul had reached this measure of humility, for I knew from it that it had steps [to climb] among those standing, since it had mastered this attribute to the point that it felt nothing at all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 3:55-4: And they, of blessed memory, have already said (see Sotah 5a), that these are the ones who merit resurrection, as it is written (Isaiah 26:19), "awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust" - one who made himself dust in his lifetime. And this is one who does not feel the disgrace of man - and therefore it says, "and My salvation shall be forever."

Now, its saying "who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is My law" is not, in my eyes, a mere doubling of the matter, but rather a sign hinting at whom it is speaking to - namely, believers in [divine] providence. And this is because it is known that two men standing to argue before a judge, one does not disgrace the other - and if it does happen so, the insulted one shall be silent and it shall be good in his eyes, since the disgrace of his opponent and the wickedness of his heart shall be revealed before the judge. And therefore it said "who know righteousness" - for he believes in [divine] providence, and that the Master of the whole earth hears the words of the disgracer, and shall repay him his due into his own bosom, and He shall answer on his behalf, and he leaves it to the true Hearer and Examiner of the hearts of men, who knows the matters, whether for good or its opposite - to this point, relevant here.

And with these his words we can understand what we say at the end of our prayer, in "my God, guard my tongue from evil," and so on, "and to those who curse my soul, let my soul be silent" - for at first glance it would have sufficed to say "let it be silent," and why "my soul"? And likewise afterward it repeats and says "and let my soul be like dust to all." Rather, the intent is to make known to us that lowliness should be embedded in the soul in such a manner that the soul itself be the silent one - for it is already possible that he not respond to his own disgrace, yet retain hatred stored in his heart, along the lines of (Genesis 27:41), "and Esau harbored a grudge against Jacob, and Esau said in his heart, let the days of mourning for my father draw near," and so on - and Scripture says (Proverbs 16:5), "every proud heart is an abomination to the LORD," even if the pride is in the heart and he does not utter it with his mouth - therefore it said "let my soul be silent," that the soul itself, from its own nature, be silent - and this is like "the people in whose heart is My law," which the pious author, of blessed memory, explained, and like the parable of the man dwelling in a city whose merchants are princes, and so on - and so we explained in the Gate of Love, that all pride and anger come only from the side of matter, for the soul, by its own nature, is lowly before the Creator and before everything, as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 16:7), "and what are we?"

And it said further, "and let my soul be like dust to all" - explaining what it said, "let my soul be silent." How can the soul be silent and not feel it? By already being so accustomed to receiving disgrace, like dust, which is prepared to constantly receive the trampling of people upon it.

And the sage, His Honor Rabbi Avraham HaLevi, may his Rock and Redeemer preserve him, said that we should learn the attribute of humility from dust - for dust, as long as it is coarse, is of no use for a craft, and all the more so for making a vessel from it; but the more it is ground fine, the better it is - so too a person. And I say that this is why it said, "and let my soul be like dust to all," for the more he accepts disgrace, the higher his soul shall rise.

And I found that His Honor Rabbi Shlomo Alkabetz, may his Rock and Redeemer preserve him, wrote concerning "and to those who curse my soul, let my soul be silent," an explanation like what I have written. And concerning "and my soul like dust," he wrote: and not this alone, but he shall clothe himself in a garment of humility to the point that he resembles his Maker, whom people sin against, yet He does them good - along the lines of (Nehemiah 9:20), "and You did not withhold Your manna from their mouth" on the day they said, "this is your god, O Israel" (see verse 18, Exodus 32:4) - therefore it said "and my soul like dust to all," for everyone tramples it, yet it raises up for them grain, bread, and food - to this point.

And so, along these lines, the pious author mentioned wrote, on the mishnah "be not easily angered" (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 10) - a fitting explanation on the verse (Ecclesiastes 7:9), "for anger rests in the bosom of fools" - and it corresponds to this teaching, saying that fools, because of the lightness of their anger and their swiftness to anger, anger dwells with them as though it had pitched its tent there - but with the intelligent person it does not "rest," but rather immediately passes. And the meaning of "bosom" is that their anger is hidden and they do not reveal it - to this point, the substance of his words. And this is "and to those who curse my soul, let my soul be silent," as explained.

Further, there he explained another explanation on this verse, along the lines of the explanation of "the people in whose heart is My law" that we have written, and he said, on the mishnah "if I am not for myself, who is for me?" (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 14), in the name of Rabbi Yosef ibn Shoshan, of blessed memory - and further he wrote that this sage was said of him that he never became angry in his days, and this was so because he never had leisure to become angry at all, being occupied with seeking the life of the soul - and over what should he be angry, when all kinds of anger and rage come over bodily matters? And therefore it said (Isaiah 51:7), "listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is My law; fear not the disgrace of man," as we have already explained - and therefore it said, "anger rests in the bosom of fools," for their heart is hidden from intellect, and therefore it does not rise up to anger. And how noble is their saying, "whoever becomes angry is as though he worships idolatry," which indicates that his thoughts are far from his own essence - to this point.
There are further matters fitting to consider so that one not become angry, and we shall explain them in a chapter of their own, in order to give some space between chapter and chapter:

The great cause that prevents anger, hatred, and envy from the heart is when a person considers, in his mind, fulfilling the mitzvah (Leviticus 19:18), "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself," which is a positive commandment including several other mitzvot, as it says in the chapter "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 31a), concerning that convert who came to convert before Hillel and said to him, teach me the whole Torah while I stand on one foot - and he said to him, "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself" - what is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow. And when a person considers this, he shall not disgrace his fellow nor insult him, just as he wishes for himself that no one disgrace him - and likewise he shall not respond to his own disgrace, just as, were it the reverse and he were the disgracer, he would not wish to be responded to - and likewise to judge his fellow favorably, and likewise the mitzvot of not taking vengeance and not bearing a grudge, which, when a person fulfills them, he must necessarily overlook wrongs against himself and purify his heart from hatred entirely - behold, by the law of Torah a person is compelled to be humble.

And because love of fellows, distancing from strife, and pursuing peace are the causes that bring a person to humility, I have seen fit to copy here the chapter on "love of fellows" that Rabbi Yisrael, peace be upon him, wrote in his Sefer Menorat HaMaor - these are its words: "you shall not hate your brother in your heart... you shall not take vengeance nor bear a grudge," and so on (Leviticus 19:17-18). Our Rabbis taught: "you shall not hate your brother" - one might think he may not strike him or curse him; therefore Scripture says "in your heart" - it is of hatred in the heart that Scripture speaks. And we learn in Tractate Yoma (23a), it is taught: what is vengeance and what is grudge-bearing? Vengeance - he said to him, lend me your sickle; he said, no. The next day his fellow said to him, lend me your axe; he said to him, I will not lend to you, just as you did not lend to me - this is vengeance. And what is grudge-bearing? He said to him, lend me your axe; he said to him, fine - I will not do like you, who did not lend to me - this is grudge-bearing.

Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says, love peace and hate strife - for even idol worshippers, as it were, are not touched by the Shechinah's [judgment] when they are at peace, as it is said (Hosea 4:17), "Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone" - but if there is strife among them, what is said of them? (ibid. 10:2), "their heart is divided; now they shall bear their guilt."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:17-2: A person should always associate with the good and upright, and distance himself from the company of the wicked and worthless people, as we learn (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 7): Nittai the Arbelite says, distance yourself from a bad neighbor, and do not associate with a wicked person - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Avot DeRabbi Natan 9:1) - whether a neighbor inside the house, or a neighbor outside, or a neighbor in the field - for afflictions come only upon the house of that wicked person, and cause the wall of the righteous person to be demolished too. How so? A wall between a wicked person and a righteous person, and a plague is seen in the wicked person's house - they demolish the righteous person's house because of the wicked person's plague. Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says, woe to the wicked, woe to his neighbor - the wicked person's sins caused the righteous person's wall to be demolished.

Another explanation: "and do not associate with a wicked person" (ibid. 9:4) - a person should not associate with an evil man, for Jehoshaphat associated with Ahab and went up with him to Ramoth-Gilead, and wrath went out against him, as it is said (II Chronicles 19:2), "should you help the wicked," and so on; and again he associated with Achazyahu, and the LORD broke his deeds, as it is said (ibid. 20:37), "because you have associated with Achazyahu, the LORD has broken your deeds." And so we find with Amnon, who associated with Yonadav, who counseled him with evil counsels, as it is said (II Samuel 13:3), "and Amnon had a friend whose name was Yonadav," and so on, and he was wise for wickedness.

And we learn in Avot DeRabbi Natan: if the young tell you, build the synagogue, do not listen to them; but if the elders tell you, come let us demolish the synagogue, listen to them - why? Because the building of the young is demolition, and the demolition of the elders is building - proof of this is the counsel of Rehoboam son of Solomon, who abandoned the counsel of the elders and took the counsel of the young.

Do not be a companion to a wicked person, even for matters of Torah, but rather a person should strive to acquire a good companion and distance himself from a bad companion - as we learn in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 25): "he who walks with the wise shall become wise" (Proverbs 13:20) - to what is this comparable? To one who enters a spice shop: even if he did not give or take anything, he takes away a good scent. So too whoever walks with the righteous takes from their ways and their good deeds. "But a companion of fools shall be harmed" - to what is this comparable? To a person who enters a tannery: even if he did not give or take anything, he takes away a bad odor. So too whoever walks with the wicked takes from their ways and their deeds.

The author said, to what is this matter comparable? To two people walking on a road who encountered two groups of people also walking on the road. One group consisted of righteous, upright, God-fearing men - one of the two joined them, and whoever saw him with them thought he was one of them; once they reached the city, he parted from them and entered the city, and they continued on. The second group consisted of worthless men, thieves and murderers, who robbed the possessions of whomever they found on the road - the second man joined them and walked with them, and whoever saw him on the road thought he was one of them; once they reached the city, he parted from them and entered the city, and they went on their way. Two men were coming to the city, and were themselves from that city - the first of them saw the group of righteous men and that man among them, and was telling the people of the city, I saw men on the road, a group of holy, pious men, and I begged them to enter the city so that the people of the city might honor them, but they did not want to; and while he was speaking, behold, that man who had joined them on the road and parted from them near the city was passing by - he said, this man is from that group of righteous men - immediately they gave him great honor and appointed him as their head, all because he had associated with the good. The second man was coming to the city and saw those thieves and robbers - he immediately became terrified and feared for his life and hid until they passed; and once he entered the city, he was telling the people of the city, I saw on the road a band of thieves, and they were killing whomever they found and plundering his money - and while he was speaking, behold, that man who had joined them on the road and parted from them near the city was passing by - he said, this man is from that band of thieves - immediately they seized him and hanged him, all because he had associated with the wicked, even though he had not stolen or plundered with them, and he died a strange death - to this point.

And whoever wishes to distance himself from transgressions should distance himself from the company of the wicked - and the sages of ethics said, when you wish to inquire about a person, ask whom he associates with, for every person acts like his fellow's deeds - therefore a person should associate with the good and distance himself from the company of the wicked and the evil. And the sage said, the company of the good is honor and glory, and the company of the vile is disgrace and shame. And whoever associates with the good is like one who carries myrrh: even if he gives none of it to his fellow, he benefits from it; and whoever associates with the wicked is like a person close to a burning furnace: even if he is not burned, he is scorched. And they further said, a person never associates with the wicked and parts from them in peace.
And always, every kind clings to its own kind: the righteous cling to the righteous, and the wicked cling to the wicked, along the lines of (Leviticus 11:15), "every raven after its kind."

And we learn in Bava Kama (92b): people have a saying, a bad palm tree travels and goes to the nest of the sarcha [some bird or bad tree]. Explanation: the bad palm tree, which bears no fruit, associates with barren trees that bear no fruit, and is happy among them. And this matter is written in the Torah, repeated in the Prophets, and stated a third time in the Writings. Written in the Torah (Genesis 28:9), "and Esau went to Ishmael." Repeated in the Prophets (Judges 11:3), "and worthless men gathered to Jephthah." And stated a third time in the Writings, "every bird dwells with its own kind, and man with his like" - though this is not found in [canonical] Scripture, but in the Book of Ben Sira, and it said "written" because it is [also elsewhere] written.

And whoever wishes to know his fellow's character should observe what he praises: if he praises good things, it is known that he is a person of good character, and if the opposite, the opposite - and this is what is written (Proverbs 27:21), "the refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, and a man is according to his praise" - he praises only according to his own character, whether bad or good.

There are six things a person cannot do, and these are they: one, there is no person who pursues the fulfillment of his desire without sinning. Two, there is no person who constantly converses with women without coming to adultery. Three, there is no person who gathers much wealth without his heart becoming proud over it. Four, there is no person who associates with the wicked and parts from them in peace. Five, there is no person who draws close to kings without the times turning against him. Six, there is no person who requests anything from vile people and has his request fulfilled. And the company of the good is entirely beneficial without harm, even if they give him nothing of their own, and even if they do not intercede on their companions' behalf - even so their company is good and beneficial, since people honor them - and therefore a person should associate with the good. And the sage said, whoever associates with the good, his own level and his family's level shall rise; and whoever associates with the wicked shall eventually become like them, and a wicked man who associates with the righteous shall eventually become like them, as it is said (Proverbs 13:20), "he who walks with the wise shall become wise." And a person should always be a servant to the generous and the good, and not a prince or judge over the light and the lowly, as we learn (Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 15), be a tail to lions and not a head to foxes.

Rabbi says, when Lot went with Abraham our father, peace be upon him, he learned from his ways and his good deeds - what did Abraham do? He made a lodging house in Charan, and whoever entered he would feed and give drink, and say to him, the God of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, blessed be His Name, is One - and when Lot came [to his own place], he did the same.

And further the sage said, it is not fitting for an intelligent person to associate with a person until he examines whether he is fit for companionship or not. And further he said, companionship is of four kinds: the love of companions resembles food. The first: a person's companionship with his wife and children, as it is said (Proverbs 5:19), "may you always be intoxicated with her love" - and just as a person always needs food, by which his body is sustained, so is a person's companionship with his wife and children always [needed] - just as every single day he needs to see them, and through them he has quiet, tranquility, and settled mind. And from where do we know that a person's wife and children are compared to food? As it is said (Psalms 128:3), "your wife shall be like a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your house; your children like olive shoots" - he compared the wife and children to a table. The second resembles medicine, and this is the companionship of a brother - for just as a person needs medicine only at a time of illness, so the companionship of a brother is needed only at a time of distress and trouble, as it is said (Proverbs 17:17), "and a brother is born for adversity." The third: the companionship of good friends, and their love and compassion resembles a father's compassion for a son - of a father it is written (Malachi 3:17), "as a man spares his son who serves him," and it is written (Psalms 103:13), "as a father has compassion on his children" - and of a friend it is written (Job 19:21), "have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends." The fourth resembles a deadly poison, and this is the companionship of the wicked, evil, and worthless people - for just as a deadly poison harms and kills, so such friends harm and kill.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:29-4: And we learn in the Midrash: whoever associates with a wicked person robs himself of this world and the World to Come; and whoever shows a pleasant face to a wicked person is among those who provoke God; and whoever deceives shall mourn in his own body; and whoever turns his fellow from a good path to an evil path dies in the midst of his days; and whoever mocks the mitzvot receives no mercy from Heaven; and whoever accustoms himself to reddening his fellow's face [with shame], his account is open against him that very day, and so on - as is found in the Pearl of Rabbi Meir, which we copied in the Gate of Fear, chapter 12.

There are fifteen things a good companion must do for his faithful friend, and then his companionship shall be fine and complete without deceit, and these are they: one, he shall greet him first. Two, he must invite his friend to all his good occasions. Three, and on his day of joy. Four, he shall guard his friend's secret and not reveal it. Five, he shall be a helper to him at his time of trouble. Six, he shall visit him in his illness and strive to attend to his needs all the days of his illness. Seven, he shall attend to his burial needs if he dies. Eight, he shall correct his words in his presence, and all the more so not in his presence [i.e., he shall not slander him behind his back, but correct gently to his face]. Nine, he shall overlook all the wrongs his friend committed against him and forgive him immediately. Ten, he shall rebuke him if he knows he has done something improper. Eleven, he shall honor him immediately. Twelve, he shall not deceive him in business dealings. Thirteen, he shall do everything he vowed to do for him. Fourteen, he shall not lie to him. Fifteen, he shall always seek mercy for him and seek his welfare in his heart.

And we learn in Avot DeRabbi Natan (see chapter 15, section 1): further, Rabbi Eliezer used to say two things: let your fellow's honor be as dear to you as your own; be careful of the honor of his sons and daughters. If you wish that no one take what is yours, do not take what is your fellow's. If you wish that nothing be said against you, do not say anything against your fellow.

Hillel says, be among the disciples of Aaron, loving peace and pursuing peace, loving fellow creatures and drawing them near to Torah. A person is obligated to love his fellow and give him honor - and is this not an a fortiori argument? If the ministering angels, among whom there is no evil inclination, give honor one to another, flesh and blood, among whom there is an evil inclination, all the more so - as it is said (Isaiah 6:3), "and one called to another and said" - one says to his fellow, you are greater than I, and you shall open with the praise of the Omnipresent first.

And we learn in Megillat Chasidim (see Avot DeRabbi Natan Zuta, chapter 2): if you wish to be attached to a friend, do business favorably for him. And a person should not act against his fellow's wishes, and should set aside his own will for the will of others, as we learn in Tractate Shabbat (118b): Rabbi Yosei said, in my days I never acted against my fellows' opinion - I know that I am not a Kohen, but had my fellows told me to go up to the platform [for the priestly blessing], I would have gone up.

There are eight kinds of company among people, and whoever associates with one learns a distinct attribute from it, and these are they: one, whoever associates with kings learns violence and pride. Two, whoever associates with the wealthy learns love of money and the pleasure of this world. Three, whoever associates with the humble learns humility, praise, and thanksgiving. Four, whoever associates with women learns lewdness, desire, laughter, vulgar speech, and every evil thought. Five, whoever associates with the young learns idle talk and jesting, as we learn (Avot, chapter 3, mishnah 10), "the chatter of children and sitting in the assemblies of the ignorant remove a person from the world." Six, whoever associates with the wicked learns sins and transgressions and removes repentance from himself. Seven, whoever associates with scoffers learns vanity and falsehood. Eight, whoever associates with the pious and righteous learns kindness and good attributes and inherits the World to Come. A person should always strive to acquire a companion for himself - if he finds one for free, [good], and if not, he should acquire one with money, as we learn (ibid., chapter 1, mishnah 6), "make for yourself a teacher and acquire for yourself a companion." And the sage said, I marvel that a person acquires slaves with his money - how does he not acquire free men with good words from his mouth, since a person acquires companions more through good words than through money?

And the early pious ones would judge every person favorably, and even if they saw a person doing something that appeared to many to be a transgression, they would not disgrace him in their hearts, but would judge him favorably and say, perhaps he did not transgress and his intent was for something else - and they would remove themselves from suspicion, for whoever suspects the upright is afflicted in his own body (Shabbat 97a). And we learn in Tractate Shabbat (127b): our Rabbis taught, whoever judges his fellow favorably is judged favorably [by Heaven] - there was a story of a certain man from Upper Galilee, and so on; see there. And further, a story of Rabbi Yehoshua, and so on; see there.

And we learn in Avot DeRabbi Natan: and judge every person favorably - there was a story of a man who sent his son to his fellow and said, tell him, my father says, lend me a measure of wheat. He went and found him measuring wheat, and he said, I have none. He came and told his father, who said, perhaps it is tithe-wheat. He further said to him, go tell him, my father says, lend me one maneh. He went and found him counting money, and he said, I have none. He came and told his father, who said, perhaps it is a deposit held for someone else. Once they met each other in the marketplace, his fellow said to him, when your son came and found me measuring wheat and I did not give it to you, what did you suspect me of? He said, perhaps it is tithe-wheat. And when he found me counting money, what did you suspect me of? He said, perhaps it is a deposit held for someone else. He said to him, by the [divine] service, so it was, and you did not deviate right or left - and of you it is said, judge every person favorably, and just as you judged me favorably, so may the Holy One, blessed be He, judge you favorably.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, whoever suspects the upright is afflicted in his own body (Shabbat 97a) - from where do we know this? From Moses, who said (Exodus 4:1), "but behold, they will not believe me" - yet before Heaven it was revealed that they would believe, as it is said (ibid. 4:31), "and the people believed." And since he suspected them, Moses was immediately punished, as it is written (ibid. 4:6), "and the LORD said to him further" - and was there no other thing but tzara'at upon his body? Rather, from here we learn that he was punished for this matter. Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina: a measure of good comes more quickly than a measure of punishment - for there (ibid.), "and he took it out, and behold, his hand was leprous, like snow" - behold, in the measure of punishment there was a delay, and it says "and behold, his hand was leprous," but in the measure of good there was no delay, and it does not say "and behold, his hand," but rather "and behold, it had returned like his own flesh" (ibid. 4:7).

And whoever is suspected of something and it is not in him needs to remove himself from the suspicion (see Berachot 31b) - for so we find with Chanah, of whom Eli said (I Samuel 1:14-15), "how long will you be drunk?" and she said to him, no, my lord, I am a woman of sorrowful spirit; I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink" - and immediately he said to her, go in peace - from here we learn that when a person is suspected of a matter and it is not in him, one must appease him, and moreover, that one must seek mercy for him, as it is said (ibid. 1:17), "and may the God of Israel grant your request" (Berachot, there). Rabbi Yosei said, may my portion be with whoever is suspected of a matter and it is not in him (Shabbat 118b).

And whoever loves his fellow shall always judge him favorably and cover his transgressions, but if he hates him, he shall always judge him unfavorably, even if he has not transgressed, and shall not see merit in him even if he is upright - and from this comes strife with him and he shall seek complaints against him, as it is said (Proverbs 10:12), "hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all transgressions" - for out of his hatred of him, his fellow's words are exaggerated in his eyes and he quarrels with him over nothing, and it is the opposite if he loves him, even if his fellow is bound to him by covenant and oath - he shall turn back and break the covenant, since the hatred hidden in his heart shall search out quarrels and stir up strife and all hatred and rivalry, and he shall think in his heart that his fellow too hates him, since he judges the hearts of people to be as evil as his own evil heart, and evil imaginings in his own heart he shall think are so in others' hearts too, and from the evil thought he shall come to action and hate his fellow creatures.
